## Observations

1. The input gives \(N\), followed by two strings \(S\) and \(T\), each of length \(N\).
2. Each position contributes one to the Hamming distance if its characters differ, and zero otherwise.
3. A single pass checks all \(N\) positions, and only a running count needs to be kept in addition to the input strings.

## Solution sketch

1. “The input gives \(N\), followed by two strings \(S\) and \(T\), each of length \(N\).” Read the three input lines in that order. The length guarantee ensures that both strings have a character at every position from \(1\) through \(N\).
2. “Each position contributes one to the Hamming distance if its characters differ, and zero otherwise.” Start the count at zero. Compare the characters at each corresponding position and increment the count only when they differ. After the scan, print the count. Identical strings produce \(0\), strings that differ everywhere produce \(N\), and when \(N=1\) the single comparison determines the answer.
3. “A single pass checks all \(N\) positions, and only a running count needs to be kept in addition to the input strings.” The algorithm takes \(O(N)\) time and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space, or \(O(N)\) space including the input strings.
